# Slides
All tools named below live on the `slides` MCP server: call them with the `mcp` tool using `server: "slides"` and the bare tool name (`slides/present` in this document means `server: "slides"`, `name: "present"`).

The Slides addon exposes presentation creation and live preview through its runtime MCP server. The working model is a tool-owned manifest with a per-slide lifecycle, structural edits through one organize tool, and a present-time completion gate. `slides/present` is the delivery gate for every mode; for pptx decks it additionally re-validates every XML file before delivery.

## Skill files
This skill is a directory of three files. The two reference files live NEXT TO this SKILL.md, in the skill's own install directory — they are part of the skill, not of any deck, and are never found in a deck's project directory:

```
<skill install dir>/
├── SKILL.md            # this file — model, tools, lifecycle, workflow
├── html-syntax.md      # HTML mode authoring rules — read before writing any <id>.html
└── pptx-xml-syntax.md  # pptx mode rules & procedure — read before writing design.xml or any <id>.xml
```

## Core rules
- **The manifest is tool-owned. NEVER hand-edit `project.json`.** Slide order, outline, and per-slide state are managed by `init_slides`, `generate_image_slide`, `organize_slides`, and native file writes. For HTML decks author only the registered `<id>.html` files with the native file tool; for image decks author only through `slides/generate_image_slide`; for pptx decks author only `design.xml` and the registered `<id>.xml` files with the native file tool.
- **For HTML and pptx decks, author through the native file `write` / `edit` tools — `write` carries one complete page document per call; `edit` applies targeted fixes to an already-written page.** These calls trigger the Slides file-edit hook to sync content, validate pptx XML, measure HTML height, and (for templated decks) inject the next page's template block. Shell commands or scripts bypass that processing and must not be the authoring workflow. If the hook was unavailable or interrupted, `slides/present` can still recover registered page files from disk and deliver them; this fallback does NOT prove hook validation or automatic repair succeeded. Review any reported issues and disclose unresolved problems instead of claiming the deck passed validation. Missing pages still block delivery, and pptx `present` independently validates every file. Never `append` to page files: appending produces a concatenated, broken document.
- **A session may contain multiple independent decks; each deck is initialized only once.** A new `slides/init_slides` call creates another deck with a new `project_id`. Use `slides/organize_slides` for structural changes — never re-init an existing deck.
- **Interrupted call recovery: verify before re-running.** If a Slides call fails with a transport error saying the operation MAY have already completed, do not immediately re-run it — a blind re-init creates a duplicate deck. First inspect the configured Slides project root: each deck lives in one directory named by its `project_id`. If the deck's directory already exists, reconnect with `slides/attach_slides("manus-resource://manus-slides/deck/<project_id>")` and continue from its returned state; re-run `slides/init_slides` only when no directory for the deck exists, or when `attach_slides` fails because the Slides service does not know the deck — that means the interrupted init never finished registering remotely, so a fresh init is the correct recovery.
- **`project_id` is mandatory for every Slides operation on an existing deck.** Persist the exact value returned by init/attach and pass it to every subsequent call for that deck.
- **Errors over fallbacks.** The tools fail loudly on missing, empty, or unknown `project_id`, unknown slides, out-of-range slide numbers, incomplete reorder sets, and pending slides at present time. Read the error and self-correct; do not work around it.
- **Templates are id-driven.** Only when the task context or the user provides an exact `template_id` (for example `Template: <id>` from the Slides New Session scene): call `slides/get_template(template_id)` once BEFORE `slides/init_slides`, tag each outline entry with a `slide_template_key` from the returned page catalog, and pass the same `template_id` to `init_slides`. No id — no template step: `get_template` cannot browse or search templates, and generic style wishes ("use a nice template") belong in `style_request`, not here.

## Per-slide lifecycle
Each slide carries a `state`:
- `edit_pending` — registered in the outline but not yet authored (the `<id>.html` / `<id>.xml` file does not exist until you write it). `init_slides` and `organize_slides add` create slides in this state.
- `edited` — the page has been authored (HTML/pptx file written, or image generated). `slides/present` refuses to deliver while any slide is still `edit_pending`. In pptx mode `edited` does NOT mean valid: fix any XML validation issues the write result reports — `slides/present` re-validates everything and fails until all files pass.

"What's left to do" is always computable from the registered outline. Image-generation results return the deck id and generated image path, and explicitly say when the deck is ready to present; they do not nominate the next page.

## Deck model
A deck is a set of per-slide files plus a tool-owned `project.json`. Choose ONE authoring mode at init via `generate_mode` and do not mix them; pick by what the user needs. Each mode's authoring rules live in its own reference file — read that file before writing.

Mode selection order: the user's own words win; otherwise a Slides scene `mode` parameter in the task context (for example `Here is the extra request from user: {"mode":"html",...}` from the Slides entry) is the user's selection — initialize with exactly that mode; otherwise an official template's required mode applies; otherwise use pptx. The scene `mode` parameter selects the authoring mode ONLY. It is never a request for a file: `{"mode":"pptx"}` means "author in pptx mode", not "give me a .pptx file" (see `slides/export`).

- **PPTX mode** (`generate_mode: "pptx"`, default) — native PowerPoint-structured slides authored as manus-pptx XML. The user views and edits the deck in the Slides studio through the delivered resource link; choosing this mode does NOT produce or imply a `.pptx` file deliverable. When the user does ask for a PowerPoint file, a pptx deck exports to a native, editable `.pptx` that opens in PowerPoint. Use it unless HTML or image mode applies. If `pptx` is not offered in this session (absent from the `generate_mode` enum), use HTML mode instead. Author with the native file `write` tool. Rules and procedure: **`pptx-xml-syntax.md`**.
- **HTML mode** (`generate_mode: "html"`) — hand-authored, self-contained HTML slides with full layout control. Use it ONLY when the user explicitly asks for HTML slides/output, when the Slides scene `mode` parameter is `html`, when an official HTML template requires it, or when pptx is not offered in this session. Author each `<id>.html` with the native file `write` tool. Rules: **`html-syntax.md`**.
- **Image mode** (`generate_mode: "image"`) — each slide is a full-bleed AI-generated image produced by `slides/generate_image_slide`: the first page alone to lock the style, then the remaining pages in parallel; best for highly visual or illustrative decks. No native file writes; see the tool below.

Use real, verifiable information; never fabricate data, citations, or authoritative claims.

## Visuals (pptx and HTML decks)
Rich, on-theme imagery is what makes a deck feel finished. Generate it proactively with `slides/generate_fast_cheap_image` — a fast, low-cost image model whose quality is good enough for slide backgrounds and illustrations, so do not ration it:
- Imagery is encouraged, not mandatory. When the design brief has a Slide Map, it decides which pages carry an image and which layout each uses (its `image` and `image layout` columns), and the brief's **Image frames** section — computed by the add-on from those layout ids — lists every frame's exact box and `aspect_ratio` plus the text boxes of that layout: generate one image per listed frame with exactly that ratio, place it in that box, put the page text in the listed text boxes, and don't add or drop images unless the user asks.
- When a page has no Image frames row (the brief was unavailable, the user asked for a different layout, or the page was added later) — except in templated decks, which keep the template's own image slots — pick a layout from **`image-layouts.md`** and use its frames and text boxes the same way. Without a Slide Map, give most pages an image where it helps and doesn't hurt legibility: structural pages (cover, section dividers, closing) get a full-bleed layout; content pages get a side, inset or band layout; pages dominated by a chart or table, or packed with text, stay image-free.
- Plan the images right after `slides/init_slides` — one per frame, so a multi-image layout needs one distinct image for each of its frames — then generate them with as few `slides/generate_fast_cheap_image` calls as possible — fill each call's `images` list (up to 4 per call; they run concurrently inside the tool — never one call per image, with one exception: when the same product, character or mascot recurs across images and the user gave no image of it, generate its first image alone, then pass that file in `references` of every later image of it) — BEFORE writing the pages that use them, so each page write can reference the returned absolute paths. For example, 10 images take three calls (4 + 4 + 2), or 1 + 4 + 4 + 1 when the first is a recurring subject's image.
- Prompt for subject, composition, art style, and the deck palette (from the design brief); ask for no text, letters, or logos. Only overlay layouts (marked `(overlay)` in Image frames: full-bleed, kpi-over, texture, overlap-card) put text on the image — for those, describe where the text box sits as calm, uncluttered space and keep the subject on the other side. Every other layout places the image beside the text: compose the subject centred and filling the frame, with no empty area reserved for text. Keep one art style across the deck — pass an earlier generated image in `references` to hold it.
- For deck visuals use this tool instead of any general-purpose image generation tool: those run premium models that are slower and more expensive than slide imagery needs. Use premium image generation only when the user explicitly asks for high-fidelity imagery. Real people, products, places, logos, and screenshots come from the user's own images or real searched images; charts are built natively. To show the user's product, character or mascot in a new scene, pass the user's image in `references` of that image so the model draws it into the scene — never paste a cutout onto a generated empty scene; use the user's image itself only where it stands alone (cover hero, detail close-up), on one or two pages. Everywhere else the subject appears — also when the user asks that it look exactly like the photo — generate a new scene for each page (setting, light, angle, props, in the deck's mood) with the user's image in `references`, which keeps the subject consistent; never fill pages with crops, blurs or tinted copies of that one photo. A request about how its images are made — no AI or generated images of it, only the user's photo — is different: then use only their photo.
- Before writing a page with an overlay layout, `read` its generated image and put the text block where the image is actually quiet — if the calm area came out on the other side, mirror the text box there instead of regenerating — and keep the text readable with the scrim, fade or panel the layout names (pptx background `overlay`, HTML gradient overlay). Behind body or small text (under 24 px) that panel or scrim must be at least 90% opaque — a see-through panel lets the photo show through and drops the text below 4.5:1; the calm area alone is not enough. Every frame gets its own image: never place one image on several pages or split one image across frames with `background-position` or crops. Templated decks keep the template's image slots: replace existing images, never add new ones, and generate each replacement at the supported `aspect_ratio` closest to that slot's width and height.

## Templated decks (official templates)

- `slides/get_template(template_id)` returns the template's style description plus a per-page catalog `{page ID, description}`. HTML is intentionally not returned there: each template page's HTML is injected for you page by page — the cover page's template HTML arrives in the `init_slides` result, and each file write's hook result carries the NEXT pending slide's template HTML.
- **Read the template page before writing the page.** For every page of a templated HTML deck, first read the injected template HTML for that slide's `slide_template_key`, then author `<id>.html` against it: the cover's template block is in the `slides/init_slides` result; each later page's block is in the result of the PREVIOUS page's file write; a page added with `slides/organize_slides` gets its block in that organize `add` result (tag every added slide with a valid `slide_template_key` — see Tools). Never author a templated page from the `get_template` catalog description alone or from memory of another page. Because injection runs one page ahead in outline order, author templated HTML decks sequentially — one file write at a time, reading each result's template block before writing the next page; the parallel authoring allowed for other decks does not apply. If no template block is available for a pending page (for example after `slides/attach_slides` in a later session), match the established layout, colors, and fonts of the deck's already-authored pages.
- When authoring a templated HTML deck, **only replace the content of the injected template page; strictly keep its layout, visual style, color palette, fonts, and special elements like logos.** Do not add images where the template has none; only replace images that already exist in the template.
- Template asset files are extracted to `assets/` inside the deck project directory at init. The injected template HTML may contain relative `./assets/...` references; rewrite every retained template asset reference to the corresponding absolute path under the exact `project_dir` returned by `slides/init_slides`, and never leave a relative asset path in an authored page.
- HTML-page templates require `generate_mode: "html"`, even when the user did not ask for HTML.
- Image-style templates require `generate_mode: "image"` and use their reference image as the sole template-style source. `init_slides` saves it under the deck's `references/` directory and returns the exact path; include that absolute path in `references` for EVERY page. From the second page on, also include the first generated slide image for continuity (two references total).
- Decks without a template (`deck-stage-basic` or no template context) are unaffected by all of the above.

## Tools
- `slides/get_template(template_id)` — fetch an official template's style description and page catalog by exact id, once per deck before `slides/init_slides`. Usage gate: see Core rules.
- `slides/init_slides(title, outline, generate_mode)` — create a new independent deck and register ALL pages up front. Always pass `generate_mode` explicitly: `pptx` (default), `html`, or `image`, chosen per Deck model above; image mode always uses `gpt-image` and `init_slides` has no model parameter. Pass `outline: [{id, title, summary, slide_template_key?}]` to register one page per entry (`<id>.html`, or `<id>.xml` in pptx mode), each `edit_pending`; no page files are written at init — for HTML and pptx decks you author each file afterwards with the native file tool, for image decks each page is produced by `slides/generate_image_slide`. In pptx mode `design` is a reserved id; write `design.xml` first (see `pptx-xml-syntax.md`). Unless the user explicitly asks for more, use at most 12 slides. The result's `project_id` identifies only this deck; the tool itself does not accept a `project_id`. For HTML and pptx decks initialized WITHOUT a template, the result also includes a deck-level `<design_brief>` (design concept, palette and typography tokens, per-slide layout patterns and image layouts, guardrails, and an Image frames table with each image's box and aspect ratio): follow it verbatim when authoring every page — in pptx mode encode its color/font tokens as the `design.xml` variables. A copy is saved at `<project_dir>/design.md`; it is context, not a slide file — do not read it again, edit it, or register it. The brief is session-local: `slides/attach_slides` in a later session does not restore it — study the deck's existing pages and stay consistent with their established style instead. If the result instead notes the brief was unavailable, proceed with this skill's default design guidance. Templated decks get no design brief — their design guidance is the injected template block, which always wins.
- Native file `write` / `edit` tools — the ONLY authoring channel for HTML and pptx decks: `write` one complete document per call to the exact absolute registered path; use `edit` for targeted follow-up fixes. Shell commands and Python/Node scripts bypass the file-edit hook (see Core rules), and `append` is never appropriate for page files. For pptx decks, each `.xml` write/edit is validated against the manus-pptx schema (see `pptx-xml-syntax.md`); validation problems come back in the tool result and MUST be fixed before presenting.
- `slides/generate_image_slide(project_id, slide_id | slide_number, content_prompt, references)` — generate or regenerate any registered page of an image deck with fixed `gpt-image`. Generate page 1 ALONE and wait for its result: it locks the deck's visual style (enforced for a new deck). Then generate ALL remaining pages by issuing one call per page in a single response (parallel tool calls, at most 10 per response; if more pages remain, send the next batch after these return) — the calls run concurrently, out-of-order calls are accepted, and an already generated page may be regenerated. For a templated image deck, include the absolute template reference-image path returned by `init_slides` on EVERY page; for an untemplated image deck, use `references: []` on page 1. On every later page, include page 1's absolute `generated_image_path` in `references` for visual continuity (when omitted, the tool falls back to it automatically). References accept 0–2 absolute sandbox PNG/JPEG/WebP paths. Invalid, missing, oversized, upload-failed, or expired references fail the call and are never silently dropped. A failed page does not affect other pages — re-send just that page's call. If a call fails with `[INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS]`, STOP: do not retry and do not generate the remaining pages; tell the user they need more credits.
- `slides/generate_fast_cheap_image(project_id, images: [{prompt, name?, aspect_ratio?, references?}])` — FAST & CHEAP image generation for pptx and HTML decks (backgrounds, illustrations, decorative art; see Visuals). Batch up to 4 images per call (generated concurrently); split larger sets into a few full calls, except that a recurring product, character or mascot the user gave no image of gets its first image generated alone, and that file goes in `references` of every later image of it; results come back in list order, and a failed item does not discard the others — regenerate only the failed ones. Give each item the `aspect_ratio` of the frame it will fill (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4 or 21:9; 4:1 / 1:4 only when the brief's Image frames lists them; default 16:9) — copy it from the brief's Image frames — so cover fit crops almost nothing. The image is saved under the deck's `assets/generated/` directory; reference each returned absolute `image_path` in its page file, and the file-edit hook uploads it with the page. Each item's `references` accepts 0–2 absolute local PNG/JPEG/WebP paths. Rejects image decks. If a call fails with `[INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS]`, STOP generating images and tell the user they need more credits.
- `slides/organize_slides(project_id, operation, …)` — structural changes to the identified existing deck. Use this tool, not another init call, to add pages to that deck:
  - `operation: 'add'`, `slide_data: [{slide_id, page_title, summary, slide_template_key?, position?}]` — register new `edit_pending` slides (1-based `position`, default append); author each added page afterwards through the deck's authoring path. On a templated deck give every added slide a valid `slide_template_key`: the add result injects the next pending slide's template HTML, and a keyless page gets no template block. Rejects duplicate ids.
  - `operation: 'delete'`, `slide_data: [{slide_id}]` or `[{slide_number}]` — remove slides. Errors on unknown slide.
  - `operation: 'reorder'`, `slide_data: [{slide_id}, ...]` — rebuild the order. Requires the COMPLETE active set exactly once (precise error lists Missing / Extra / Duplicate).
- `slides/write_notes(project_id, notes)` — write or update speaker notes for authored slides of the identified deck, `notes: [{slide_id | slide_number, note}]`. Partial update: slides not listed keep their notes; `note: ""` clears one. Errors on unknown slides and on slides still `edit_pending` (author content first). See the Speaker notes section for when and how to write them.
- `slides/present(project_id, title?)` — completion gate + delivery for the identified deck. First recovers registered page files from disk if the file-edit hook missed them; errors and lists any pages still missing. For pptx decks it additionally re-validates `design.xml` and every `<id>.xml` and fails with the file list + errors until all pass; otherwise returns its stable base `resource_uri`. Disk recovery is not evidence that hook checks passed. Call this last for each deck.
- `slides/export(project_id, format, version_id?, output_dir?)` — export the deck to `pdf`/`pptx`; saves the file into the sandbox and returns its absolute path. **Do NOT export by default.** The default deliverable is the deck's `manus-resource://` link from `slides/present`; the user can download from the Slides studio. Call `export` ONLY when the user has explicitly asked in this task for a downloadable PDF/PPTX file that has not been delivered yet (for example "导出 PPTX", "给我 pptx 文件", "download it as PDF"); a request made before clarifying questions or an interruption still counts. None of these is an export request: `generate_mode: "pptx"`, a Slides scene parameter such as `{"mode":"pptx"}`, the PowerPoint mode option, the words "slides" / "PPT" / "deck" / "presentation" alone, or a file exported in an earlier turn. After an edit, do not re-export unless the user asks again in that turn. Export after `slides/present`. An `in_progress` result means conversion continues server-side — retry the same call after ~30s.
- `slides/attach_slides(resource_uri)` — materialize an existing deck by its `manus-resource://...` URI and return the `project_id` required for later operations. Attaching it does not replace or select another local deck.

## Workflow
Research comes BEFORE slides: gather enough verified content (facts, figures, sources) to fill every planned page before initializing the deck — never start authoring on thin material. If while authoring a page you find it needs a visual element you don't have, get it first — a real searched image for real subjects, otherwise `slides/generate_fast_cheap_image` — then write the page.

1. Plan one deck's complete outline, then call `slides/init_slides({title, outline, generate_mode})` to register every page as `edit_pending`. Save the returned `project_id` as, for example, `deck_a_id`. Templated decks only (exact `template_id` in context — see Core rules): `slides/get_template` comes first, and the template's generate mode carries into `init_slides`.
2. Author every page following the chosen mode's rules (read its reference file first): HTML — write each `<id>.html` with the native file `write` tool (`html-syntax.md`); pptx — write `design.xml`, then each `<id>.xml` with the native file `write` tool (`pptx-xml-syntax.md`); image — call `slides/generate_image_slide` for page 1 alone, then the remaining pages in parallel (out-of-order accepted; see the tool entry below). For HTML and pptx decks, first generate the planned visuals in one parallel batch of `slides/generate_fast_cheap_image` calls (see Visuals). Before writing a page, think through design, continuity, layout, key content, and canvas fit. HTML and pptx pages are independent files, so you may author several in parallel by issuing multiple native file `write` calls in one turn — one page per call, and never author through shell commands or scripts (see Core rules). Templated HTML decks stay sequential because each page's template HTML arrives in the previous write's result; read it before writing that page (see Templated decks). For image mode, follow the registered outline rather than relying on each result to nominate the next page.
3. Call `slides/organize_slides({project_id: deck_a_id, operation: 'add' | 'delete' | 'reorder', slide_data})` for any structural change. Adding pages to deck A must use organize with `deck_a_id`; do not init again.
4. Address issues reported by the authoring tools. Do not call `slides/capture_screenshot` for model-driven QA; it is not a model-visible tool. Hook measurements and server-side cover capture are automatic.
5. Call `slides/present({project_id: deck_a_id})` — it gates on pending slides (and, for pptx decks, on `design.xml` + every page passing validation), then returns deck A's resource. Deliver it (see below).
6. To create deck B in the same session, call `slides/init_slides({title, outline, generate_mode})` again, save the new result as `deck_b_id`, and use that exact ID in every operation on B. Calls for A and B may be interleaved safely.
7. To continue an existing resource, call `slides/attach_slides({resource_uri})`, save the returned `project_id`, then continue with the deck's authoring path (native file writes for HTML and pptx, `slides/generate_image_slide` for image) plus explicit-ID organize / present calls. Other local decks remain intact.

## Speaker notes
Notes are opt-in: do NOT write speaker notes unless the user (or a host message) explicitly asks for them — creating a deck never implies notes. When asked, use `slides/write_notes` for every request about speaker notes, presenter scripts, or talking points — generating, rewriting, restyling, shortening, or clearing them. This includes host messages like "Generate speaker notes for this presentation" or "Generate speaker notes for page N" sent by the studio's generate button (page N is 1-based, matching `slide_number`).

- Notes attach to authored slides only — author a slide's content first, then write its note based on that actual content. Notes save live into the studio speaker-notes panel and presenter view and are included in PPTX exports; no re-present is needed for notes to appear.
- Regenerate, never refuse: when the user asks to (re)generate notes, always rewrite and replace the requested slides' notes. Treat an existing note as a draft — keep its strong lines, tighten the rest. Current notes are echoed in `slides/write_notes` and `slides/attach_slides` results.
- Ground every note ONLY in that slide's actual content and the deck outline. Never fabricate data, quotes, or visuals; explain what a chart or image means instead of describing it.

Default writing style (apply the user's own style/tone/length instructions when given):
- Natural speech for delivery, not formal prose: contractions, "you/we", active voice, concrete verbs; vary sentence length for rhythm and keep every sentence under 25 words.
- Per slide: open with a 1–2 sentence hook framing the key message; deliver 2–3 crisp points that interpret the content (insights over description); optionally add one connecting sentence from the previous slide and a transition toward the next (skip on the first/last slide).
- Plain text only — no Markdown, bullets, or headings. At most 200 words per slide. Write in the user's language.
- Never use meta or boilerplate openers like "This slide shows…", "As you can see…", "Today we'll…", "In this presentation…".

## Delivery contract (REQUIRED — read before finishing)
The user-facing deliverable for a Slides task is the **resource**, not images and not an exported file. `slides/present` returns the deck's stable base `resource_uri` like `manus-resource://manus-slides/deck/<project_id>` so the deck always opens the latest version.

- Your **final message MUST link every delivered deck as a Markdown link** — one ``<deck title>`` per deck, using each `slides/present` result's `resource_uri` verbatim as the href. Always use Markdown-link form; never paste a bare `manus-resource://...` URI as plain text. If you omit a link, old clients do not receive the Slides attachment.
- Deliver exactly one resource URI per deck. A short completion sentence plus one link per deck is enough.
- Do NOT call `slides/export` or add a PPTX/PDF download link or file attachment unless the user explicitly asked in this task for that file and it has not been delivered yet (see `slides/export`). The pptx authoring mode and the Slides scene `mode` parameter are not such a request.

## Boundaries
- Structural changes flow through Slides tools; page content flows through native file `write`/`edit` calls (HTML: `<id>.html`; pptx: `design.xml` and `<id>.xml`) or, for image decks, only through `slides/generate_image_slide` — never through shell commands or scripts.
- Widget actions such as refresh are host/UI actions; do not describe them as model-visible deck editing tools.
- Do NOT hand-edit `project.json`. For HTML decks write only registered slide HTML paths with the native file tool; for pptx decks write only `design.xml` and registered slide XML paths; for image decks never write slide files by hand; use `slides/organize_slides` for add/delete/reorder.

## Portability & Multi-Agent Execution Notes

This skill was canonicalized from the Mr-Agents collection for universal agent compatibility.

- **Primary Target Category:** marketing-seo
- **Required Capabilities:** filesystem, network, node, python
- **Tool Substitution:** Execute shell or python commands through your agent's native execution tool (e.g., Claude Code `Bash`, Gemini CLI terminal, Cursor terminal, Copilot workspace agent).
- **Authentication & Connectors:** Pass any required API keys or tokens via standard environment variables or MCP server configurations rather than proprietary platform connectors.
